correctness.rationale: Direct graph definitions and complete combinatorial equivalence reduce the result to finite matching enumeration and edge-set transversals. Two independently structured standard-library checkers were run from package paths: one enumerates all 120 matchings and every subset until the exact anti-forcing threshold and counts all minimizers; the other re-enumerates matchings bipartitely, checks 120 explicit graph automorphism images across eight representatives, confirms matching-specific deletion upper certificates and disjoint alternating-cycle lower certificates, then counts all minimum deletion sets for each representative. Both outputs agree on (6,93,18,3), eight refined classes and 25,092. Limitation: exact finite theorem only, no infinite generalization.

value.rationale: Anti-forcing is a natural measure of robustness/identifiability of dimer configurations by external edge deletions. Exact classification on the canonical nonplanar, symmetric cubic bipartite Nauru graph is not supplied by basic matching counts or cyclomatic bounds. The key structural distinction is that the two-factor length profile determines the anti-forcing minimum, yet two equal (6,18) profiles have different numbers of optimizers (207 versus 24); eight automorphism orbits and 25,092 minimum witness pairs are fully classified. This finite self-contained invariant and decomposition can benchmark nonplanar alternating-cycle packing and hitting.
